title: Why Is There a SAUSAGE Between Your Fingers? 🌭
description:
Touch your fingertips together near your eyes and look PAST them: a little sausage floats between them. That's you seeing double. Each eye sees your fingers from its own side, so when you look at the far wall the two pictures stop lining up, and your brain stacks them anyway. Where one eye's fingertip lands on the other eye's, you get a stub with a fingertip at each end: the sausage. Close one eye and it's gone. In fact, everything nearer or farther than what you are looking at is doubled all the time; your brain just doesn't mention it (eye doctors call it physiological double vision). The trick was written up as the "floating finger illusion" back in 1928. Did you see it?
